newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 18.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Feb. 18.

text.p: Three major Gulf of Mexico ports were reported closed Tuesday, including crude port Dos Bocas, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily meteorological report.
Ports Dos Bocas in Tabasco state and Cayo Arcas and Ciudad del Carmen in Campeche state were shut as winds from the north blew between 30 and 40 km per hour.
Port officials at Dos Bocas said the terminal should open for petroleum shipments by 1400 local/2000 GMT, as winds have relaxed and waves are still 10 to 12 feet high.
Crude port Pajaritos in Veracruz state reopened at 0600 local/1200 GMT Tuesday, on the fifth consecutive day since it was shut.
The ministry said Puerto Juarez, Salina Cruz, and Puerto Madero were shut to smaller tourism and fishing boats.
Ships were advised to exercise caution in Campeche Sound, Yucatan peninsula, western Baja California and the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of strong winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Lower temperatures, light rains and clouds in the Gulf of Tehuantepec, the west of Cuba and the Bahamas. Winds from the north and northeast at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/19 to 22 miles per hour) and waves nine to 12 feet high.
Winds between 15 and 20 kilometers per hour along majority of shore.

Disperse clouds along the gulf, with isolated rains along the coasts of Tamaulipas, Campeche Sound and the Yucatan Peninsula. Winds in the region moderate, at (19 to 28 km/11 to 19 miles per hour) with higher waves in the southern gulf region.

Cold front settled from the west of Cuba to the northeast Yucatan peninsula with light rains along coasts of Quintana Roo and Belize. Winds reported from 15 to 20 knots and waves from four to seven feet high expected to relax later in the day.
